objective: By the end of this lesson you can plan and brief a taxi like a professional, copy and read back complex clearances, read every sign, marking and light you will meet (including runway status lights and LAHSO markings), hold the controls for the wind, and taxi by day, at night and in low visibility without a runway incursion.
why: About three runway incursions happen each day at U.S. towered airports, and about 65 percent of all runway incursions are caused by pilots [[1:365|PHAK 14-31]] [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]]. As a commercial pilot you will taxi at strange airports with passengers and time pressure, so the taxi has to be planned and flown like any other phase of flight [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b]].

prereading.what: Taxi technique: speed, brake check, steering, wind control positions, instrument checks.
prereading.label: AFH Ch 2, 2-18 to 2-21

prereading.what: Single-pilot taxi SOPs: planning, briefing, written clearances, runway crossings, exterior lights.
prereading.label: AC 91-73B, pages 3-10

prereading.what: Taxi clearances, required readbacks, progressive taxi and low-visibility taxi.
prereading.label: AIM 4-3-18 to 4-3-19

prereading.what: Taxiway and holding position markings, mandatory, location and direction signs.
prereading.label: AIM 2-3-4 to 2-3-10

prereading.what: Lead-on and lead-off lights, LAHSO lights, runway status lights, taxiway lights and stop bars.
prereading.label: AIM 2-1-5 to 2-1-10

prereading.what: Land and hold short operations: pilot responsibilities, readbacks and visual aids.
prereading.label: AIM 4-3-11

prereading.what: Runway incursion avoidance, runway confusion, hold short, crossing and line up and wait instructions.
prereading.label: PHAK 14-31 to 14-35

warmup: Ground has cleared you to cross a runway. As you reach the hold line, a row of red lights is glowing in the pavement across the taxiway in front of you. Do you go? What do you do next?

key_terms.def: Any occurrence at an aerodrome involving the incorrect presence of an aircraft, vehicle or person on the protected area of a surface designated for landing and takeoff [[7:1|AC 91-73B 1]].
A kind of runway incursion where you take off or land on a taxiway or the wrong runway, usually without knowing it until afterward [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].
A place on the movement area with a history or risk of collision or runway incursion, where pilots must pay extra attention [[34:358|AIM P/CG]].
One solid and one dashed yellow line between the ramp and the movement area (the area under ATC). The dashed line is on the movement side [[33:159|AIM 2-3-6c]].
Yellow dashes on both sides of the centerline for up to 150 feet before a runway holding position marking. Get ready to stop [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]].
Land and hold short operations: landing and holding short of an intersecting runway, taxiway or other designated point [[33:253|AIM 4-3-11a]].
The runway length available to the LAHSO hold short point. Published in the Chart Supplement and Terminal Procedures; ATC gives it on request [[33:254|AIM 4-3-11b2]].
Automatic red in-pavement lights (RELs and THLs) that show a runway is unsafe to enter, cross, take off from or land on. They never give a clearance [[33:127|AIM 2-1-6a]].
A row of steady red lights across the taxiway at the runway hold, used below 1,200 feet RVR to confirm a clearance. Never cross it while lit [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10e]] [[33:134|AIM 2-1-10e]].
A pink circle with a number (or number and letter), left of the centerline on a low-visibility taxi route, that identifies where you are [[33:149|AIM 2-3-4g]].

A Part 135 rule term (14 CFR 135.100): all ground operations involving taxi, takeoff and landing, and all flight below 10,000 feet except cruise, when only safety duties are allowed [[6:33|14 CFR 135.100]]. Part 91 has no such rule, but the FAA recommends the same sterile cockpit during taxi [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.5]].

chunks.title: Plan the taxi before engine start

body.p: Treat the surface movement as a phase of flight. AC 91-73B splits taxi planning into review items and briefing items [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b]]. Use current data, not memory of the last visit.

head: Source
What you pull from it for the taxi
rows: Chart Supplement

The most complete data on a public airport, revised every 56 days. Also lists LAHSO for selected airports and has airport diagrams for selected towered airports [[1:337|PHAK 14-3]] [[1:338|PHAK 14-4]]
Airport diagram
Runways, taxiways, hot spots, LAHSO lines, ILS hold lines, nonmovement areas and run-up areas [[2:123|Chart Users' Guide, Airport Diagram Features]]
NOTAMs
Temporary, time-critical items such as taxiway and runway closures and construction [[1:338|PHAK 14-4]] [[1:339|PHAK 14-5]]
ATIS
Weather, runways in use, specific ATC procedures and construction that could affect taxi planning [[1:339|PHAK 14-5]]

body.p: A hot spot is a runway safety problem area, usually a complex or confusing taxiway/taxiway or taxiway/runway intersection. It is a brown open circle or ellipse with a number such as HS 1, which matches a description on the Hot Spot page in the front of the Terminal Procedures Publication [[2:124|Chart Users' Guide, Hot Spots]].

bullets: Brief when you will run checklists and make radio calls, so they do not clash with watching your position. If possible, run checklists only when stopped or taxiing straight with no complex intersections [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(a)]].
Brief the expected route: hold short lines, runways to cross, hot spots and other conflicts [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]].
Mark the critical spots where you need extra care: hot spots, runway crossings, and lining up for takeoff [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(f)]].
Set flaps and trim and enter the GPS flight plan before you first move [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(g)]].

callout.text: Part-time tower? Be absolutely certain whether it is open before you operate. If in doubt, call on the tower frequency [[7:13|AC 91-73B App 1, 2a]].

check.q: Where do you find the written description that goes with "HS 2" on an airport diagram?
check.a: On the Hot Spot page in the front of the Terminal Procedures Publication; the number on the diagram matches that listing [[2:124|Chart Users' Guide, Hot Spots]].

chunks.title: Taxi clearances, readbacks and radio calls

callout.text: 14 CFR 91.129(i): at an airport with an operating control tower, no person may operate an aircraft on a runway or taxiway, or take off or land, without an appropriate ATC clearance [[60:454|14 CFR 91.129(i)]]. 14 CFR 91.123(a): if you are uncertain of a clearance, ask ATC right away [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]].

body.p: First call to ground: aircraft identification, location, type of operation (VFR or IFR) and point of first intended landing, for example "Washington ground, Beechcraft One Three One Five Niner at hangar eight, ready to taxi, I-F-R to Chicago" [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18d1]]. AC 91-73B puts it as who you are, where you are, what you want and what you know (the ATIS code) [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(2)]].

head: What ATC does
What it means for you
rows: States the runway first, then the route, then any hold short or crossing [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]]
The runway assignment does NOT let you enter or cross that runway at any point [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]]
Issues an explicit clearance for every runway crossing [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]]
Crossings normally come one at a time, after you have crossed the previous runway; closely spaced runways (less than 1,000 feet apart) may be an exception [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]]
Must get a readback of all runway hold short instructions [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a7 NOTE]]
Always read back the runway assignment, any clearance to enter a specific runway, and any hold short or line up and wait instruction [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]]
Never uses the word "cleared" for taxi [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]]
Listen for "taxi via", "cross" and "hold short"

body.p: Read back with your complete call sign and the runway designator, and do not answer with "Roger" or "Wilco" [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]]. Controller: "November 477ZA, Runway four, taxi via Echo, hold short of Runway two five at Taxiway Delta." Pilot: "November 477ZA, Runway four via Echo, hold short of Runway two five at Delta" [[1:368|PHAK Figure 14-53]].

callout.text: Copy it in shorthand: "/" for hold short, "X" for cross. "Taxi 9R via Bravo, Echo, Juliet, hold short 4L at Echo" becomes "9R B E J 4L E" with the clearance limit circled [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e(2)]]. Unfamiliar or confused? Ask for progressive taxi. ATC may also give it without being asked because of traffic, construction or closed taxiways [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b3]].

body.p: Nontowered airports: self-announce on the CTAF before taxiing and before taxiing onto the runway for departure [[1:337|PHAK Figure 14-1]]. Monitor the CTAF from engine start, and say the airport name at the beginning and end of each call [[7:14|AC 91-73B App 1, 4b and 5]].

check.q: Ground says: "N52KA, Runway 1, taxi via Kilo, hold short of Runway 5." What is your readback?
check.a: "N52KA, Runway 1, hold short of Runway 5" (adding "via Kilo" is fine). Runway assignment and hold short with full call sign [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].

chunks.title: Signs: what each one tells you

body.p: Airport signs follow AC 150/5340-18H. Learn them by type, because the colors never change from airport to airport.

head: Sign type
Looks like
Tells you
rows: Mandatory instruction
White letters with black outline on red
Runway or critical-area entrance, approach/departure area, or no entry [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]]
Location
Yellow letters and yellow border on black
The taxiway or runway you are on [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]]
Direction
Black on yellow, always with arrows
Taxiways leading out of an intersection [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]]
Destination
Black on yellow, always with an arrow
General direction to a remote place [[19:12|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]]
Boundary
Black on yellow
Edge of the runway safety area or ILS critical area, for a pilot leaving the runway [[19:12|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]]
Runway distance remaining
White number on black
Runway left in thousands of feet; the last ("1") sign is at least 950 feet from the end [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]] [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]]
Taxiway ending marker
Marker at the end of a taxiway
The taxiway does not continue beyond the intersection [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]]

bullets: "15-33": Runway 15 threshold to the left, 33 to the right. Where a taxiway meets the start of the takeoff runway, only that runway number may appear [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8b1]].
A taxiway that meets the intersection of two runways shows both runways with arrows pointing toward each threshold [[33:163|AIM 2-3-8b1(b)]].

"15-APCH" or "15 APCH-33 DEP": a hold in a runway approach or departure area. When told "hold short of Runway 15 approach", no part of the airplane may pass the marking [[33:163|AIM 2-3-8b2]] [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a3]].
"ILS": hold here when ATC tells you to hold short of the ILS critical area [[33:164|AIM 2-3-8b3]].
No Entry: aircraft may not enter, for example a one-way taxiway or a vehicle roadway [[33:164|AIM 2-3-8b4]].
Runway location signs are put where runways are close enough to confuse you; use them with your compass [[33:166|AIM 2-3-9a2]].

callout.text: Red: a line you need permission to cross. Black: where you are. Yellow: where you are going, or what you have just cleared.

check.q: A red sign on your taxiway reads "33 DEP-15 APCH". What is ahead?
check.a: A holding position that protects the Runway 33 departure area and Runway 15 approach area. Stop there when ATC tells you to hold short of that area [[33:163|AIM 2-3-8b2]] [[33:164|AIM 2-3-8b2]].

body.p: Runway markings are white. Taxiway markings, closed or hazardous areas, and holding positions (even on a runway) are yellow [[33:138|AIM 2-3-2b]].

head: Marking
Looks like
What you do
rows: Taxiway centerline
One continuous yellow line
Keep it under the airplane, but it does not guarantee wingtip clearance [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b1]]
Enhanced centerline
Yellow dashes on both sides, up to 150 feet before a runway hold
Prepare to stop unless cleared onto or across [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]]. Painted only on taxiways that lead directly onto a runway [[20:74|AC 150/5340-1M 4.3]] [[20:75|AC 150/5340-1M 4.3]]
Runway holding position
Four yellow lines, two solid and two dashed
Hold on the solid side [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a]]
ILS critical area hold
Two solid lines 2 feet apart joined by pairs of lines 10 feet apart (a ladder)
Stop here when told; you are clear only when the whole airplane is past it [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5b]]
Taxiway/taxiway hold
Single dashed yellow line
Stop before it when told to hold short of that taxiway [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5c]] [[33:152|AIM 2-3-5c]]
Nonmovement area boundary
One solid and one dashed yellow line
Dashed side is the movement area, under ATC [[33:159|AIM 2-3-6c]]
Taxiway edge
Continuous double yellow, or dashed double yellow
Continuous: pavement beyond is not for aircraft. Dashed: usable pavement such as an apron [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4c]] [[33:145|AIM 2-3-4c]]
Surface painted signs
Red with white (hold) or black with yellow (location)
Hold sign is left of centerline, location sign right of centerline [[33:152|AIM 2-3-5d]] [[33:149|AIM 2-3-4f]]

callout.text: A temporarily closed runway has yellow crosses only at each end, and there may be no visual sign at all. Check NOTAMs and ATIS. Closed taxiways are usually barricaded [[33:161|AIM 2-3-6e]].

body.p: Paved taxi shoulders can look like full-strength pavement but may not hold the airplane up. Yellow shoulder markings show that pavement is not usable [[33:145|AIM 2-3-4d]].

check.q: Leaving the FBO ramp you roll over a solid yellow line and then a dashed one. What did you just do?
check.a: You entered the movement area: the solid line is on the nonmovement side [[33:159|AIM 2-3-6c]]. At a towered airport you need approval before doing this [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a]].

chunks.title: Airport lights, including runway status lights

head: Light
Looks like
Meaning
rows: Taxiway edge
Blue
Edges of the taxiway [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10a]]
Taxiway centerline
Steady green
Taxi path, mainly for low visibility [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10b]]
Lead-off / lead-on
Alternating green and yellow
You are inside the runway environment or ILS critical area [[33:126|AIM 2-1-5c, d]]
Clearance bar
Three steady yellow in-pavement lights
A taxiway holding position, or an intersecting taxiway at night [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10c]]
Runway guard lights
Pair of flashing yellow lights beside the taxiway, or a row of yellow lights across it
Taxiway/runway intersection, at the runway hold [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10d]]
Stop bar
Row of steady red lights across the taxiway, red lights on each side
Confirms the clearance to enter or cross below 1,200 feet RVR [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10e]] [[33:134|AIM 2-1-10e]]
Land and hold short lights
Row of pulsing white lights across the runway
LAHSO hold short point; on whenever LAHSO is in effect [[33:126|AIM 2-1-5e]]

callout.text: Never cross a red stop bar, even with an ATC clearance. If the lead-on lights go out after you cross a stop bar, hold your position and call ATC [[33:134|AIM 2-1-10e]].

body.p: Runway Status Lights are fully automatic and driven by surveillance systems. They do not replace or give an ATC clearance [[33:127|AIM 2-1-6a]].

bullets: Runway Entrance Lights (REL): red lights along the taxiway centerline from the hold line to the runway. Red means high-speed traffic on the runway or an aircraft on final within about 1 mile. Stop at the hold line or stay stopped, and call ATC if your clearance conflicts [[33:127|AIM 2-1-6b]].

Takeoff Hold Lights (THL): a double row of red lights on the runway, 1,500 feet long, starting 375 feet from the departure threshold. Red means the runway is occupied or about to be. Stop if you safely can [[33:128|AIM 2-1-6c]].
When THLs go out, that is not a takeoff clearance [[33:128|AIM 2-1-6c NOTE]].

check.q: You are lined up and waiting and the THLs in front of you go dark. May you start the takeoff roll?
check.a: No. THLs going out is not a takeoff clearance; all takeoff clearances come from ATC [[33:128|AIM 2-1-6c NOTE]].

body.p: Told "hold short of Runway XX"? Stop so no part of the airplane extends past the runway holding position marking. At a towered airport do not cross it without a clearance. At a nontowered airport make sure you are clear of other aircraft, vehicles and people first [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]].

bullets: Before entering or crossing any runway, be positive ATC cleared you. Scan the full length of the runway and the final approach. If anything is unclear, stop and ask [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(4)]].
Scan the runway and its approaches even after ATC has cleared you [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]].
Use extra care when taxiing between active parallel runways [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(5) CAUTION]].
Line up and wait: scan the full length and the final. If ATC gave no reason for the wait and none is visible, expect a call within 90 seconds; if none comes, call ATC [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(8), (9)]].
When cleared to cross or take off, do it without delay, and tell ATC of any expected delay [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(6)]].

Intersection departure: you are expected to taxi to (but not onto) the end of the runway unless ground approved the intersection. State your position when you call the tower [[33:253|AIM 4-3-10d, e]].
Told to use a runway as a taxiway? Do not get confused and take off on it [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].

callout.text: After landing, the whole airplane, tail included, must be past the hold line. If a parallel runway's hold line keeps you from clearing, stop and tell ATC right away. Leave flaps, trim and radio changes until you are clear of all runways [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(11), (13)]].

body.p: Nontowered or tower closed: not every aircraft has a radio. Listen on the CTAF and scan the full runway plus its approach and departure paths before you enter or cross [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(12)]].

check.q: After landing you are stopped between your runway's hold line and a parallel runway's hold line, with your tail still over the first one. What do you do?
check.a: Stop and tell ATC right away; you are not clear of your runway until the whole airplane is past its hold line [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(11)]].

body.p: LAHSO means landing and holding short of an intersecting runway, an intersecting taxiway, or another designated point [[33:253|AIM 4-3-11a]]. You may accept it only if you, as PIC, decide the airplane can land and stop within the Available Landing Distance (ALD). ALD is in the Chart Supplement and Terminal Procedures, and ATC gives it on request [[33:253|AIM 4-3-11b2]] [[33:254|AIM 4-3-11b2]].

bullets: The PIC has final authority to accept or decline, and is expected to decline if it would compromise safety [[33:254|AIM 4-3-11b3]].
Students and pilots not familiar with LAHSO should not take part [[33:254|AIM 4-3-11b2]].
Plan ahead: during preflight, decide which LAHSO combinations your airplane can use [[33:254|AIM 4-3-11b4]].

Want full length, or a different runway? Tell ATC promptly, ideally before the clearance is issued. Once accepted, you must comply unless you get an amended clearance or have an emergency; you may still go around [[33:255|AIM 4-3-11b5]].
Read back the whole clearance including "hold short of (runway, taxiway or point)", without being asked [[33:255|AIM 4-3-11b7]] [[33:256|AIM 4-3-11b7]].
LAHSO should only be issued with at least a 1,000-foot ceiling and 3 statute miles visibility [[33:256|AIM 4-3-11c5]]. That is the only weather limit in AIM 4-3-11.

PHAK only (not in AIM 4-3-11): LAHSO is generally not authorized at night and is not authorized on wet runways [[1:345|PHAK 14-11]]. The PHAK also bars solo student pilots, which matches the AIM's advice that students not take part [[33:254|AIM 4-3-11b2]].

body.p: Accepted "cleared to land Runway XX, hold short of Runway YY"? Exit before the hold markings or stop at them. With a plain "cleared to land" you may use the whole runway and ignore the LAHSO markings [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a2]]. A taxiing pilot may hear "cross runway six right at bravo, landing aircraft will hold short" and reads back "wilco, cross runway six right at bravo, landing traffic (type) to hold" [[33:256|AIM 4-3-11c2]].
LAHSO visual aids are yellow hold-short markings, red and white signs, and sometimes in-pavement lights, but not every LAHSO airport has all of them [[33:256|AIM 4-3-11c4]].

check.q: Tower says only "cleared to land Runway 27". You see LAHSO hold markings for Runway 13-31 ahead on the runway. Must you stop there?
check.a: No. With no hold short instruction you may use the full landing length and disregard the LAHSO markings [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a2]] [[1:344|PHAK 14-10]].

chunks.title: Wind: read it, then hold the controls for it

body.p: Check the wind indicators even when someone on CTAF gives you a wind, because that report may be wrong. A wind sock shows direction and lets you estimate speed and gusts. A wind tee or tetrahedron can be set by hand to the runway in use, so look at the sock too [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]]. At a towered field, use a tetrahedron only when the tower is closed; tower instructions come first [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]].

head: Wind from
Ailerons
Elevator
rows: Quartering headwind
Upwind aileron UP (yoke toward the wind)
Nosewheel: neutral. Tailwheel: full aft unless the headwind is very strong [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]]
Quartering tailwind
Upwind aileron DOWN (yoke away from the wind)
DOWN (yoke forward) [[24:56|AFH 2-19]]
Calm
Neutral; ailerons do not steer
Neutral [[24:56|AFH 2-19]]

bullets: Find the quadrant fast: wind direction minus your heading. 0 to 90 is right front, 90 to 180 right rear, 180 to 270 left rear, 270 to 360 left front (add 360 if the answer is negative).
Swerves are most likely when turning from a downwind heading toward an upwind heading, and strong wind adds weathervaning [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
Downwind: keep power to a minimum and brake only now and then; throttle at idle before braking except in sharp, slow turns [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
At night the wind is harder to feel and see, so look at the wind information during planning [[24:224|AFH 11-7]].

check.q: You are taxiing on heading 270 with the wind from 200 at 15 knots. How do you hold the yoke?
check.a: 200 - 270 = -70, plus 360 = 290: left front, a quartering headwind. Yoke turned left (left aileron up), elevator neutral [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

chunks.title: Fly it step by step to commercial standards

bullets: 1. Brief route, hot spots and crossings; finish flaps, trim and GPS entries before moving [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d), (g)]].
2. Beacon on with the engine running; navigation, position and anticollision lights on before taxi [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)(a), (b)]].
3. Add a little power to start rolling, then pull the throttle back at once so you do not speed up too much [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
4. Brake check right away: throttle back, a little pressure on one brake, then the other. If braking is poor, shut down the engine immediately [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
5. Keep speed throttle-dependent: slow enough that closing the throttle stops you promptly. Go slower on busy ramps [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
6. Steer with the rudder pedals; use brake only to tighten a turn after full pedal. Slow down before every turn [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
7. Yellow centerline under the middle of the fuselage; eyes outside, side to side and near to far [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
8. Follow your progress on the diagram and check each taxiway with the heading indicator. Always know where you are and what the next point needing attention is [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7d, 7d(1)]].

9. Check the flight instruments on the way: airspeed near zero, attitude level, altimeter at field elevation, turn indicator correct with the ball outside, heading indicator matches the compass, VSI zero [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
10. Stop short of the hold line with the nosewheel straight. Run up on a firm spot clear of the taxiway with nothing behind you [[24:57|AFH 2-20]] [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

head: ACS standard (CA.II.D)
What the examiner watches for
rows: S1: Receive and correctly read back clearances/instructions, if applicable
Runway, crossings, hold shorts and LUAW read back with full call sign, no "Roger"
S2: Use an airport diagram or taxi chart during taxi, if published, and maintain situational awareness
Diagram out, position known, next turn and hot spot anticipated
S3: Position the flight controls for the existing wind, if applicable
Correct aileron and elevator on every leg, changed after each turn
S4: Complete the appropriate checklist(s)
POH taxi items and instrument checks, done at safe moments
S5: Perform a brake check immediately after the airplane begins moving
Both brakes tested in the first few feet
S6: Maintain positive control ... without excessive use of brakes
Speed set with throttle; no riding the brakes
S7: Comply with airport/taxiway markings, signals, and ATC clearances and instructions
Follows signs, lines, lights and the clearance actually issued
S8: Position the airplane properly relative to hold lines
No part of the airplane past the hold line; fully past it when exiting

check.q: Your examiner sees you riding the brakes on a long downwind taxi. Which skill is at risk, and what is the fix?
check.a: S6, positive control without excessive brakes (ACS CA.II.D.S6). Use minimum power, brake only occasionally, and close the throttle before braking [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

callout.text: 14 CFR 91.209: from sunset to sunrise you may not operate an aircraft without lighted position lights. Day or night, if the aircraft has an anticollision light system it must be on, unless the PIC decides that turning it off is safer because of operating conditions [[60:491|14 CFR 91.209]].

head: When
Exterior lights
rows: Engine running
Rotating beacon on [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)(a)]]
Before taxi
Navigation, position, anticollision and logo lights. Taxi light on when moving, off when stopped or yielding. No strobes if they blind others [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24e]]
Taxiing on or across any runway
All exterior lights, at the PIC's discretion and within equipment limits [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24f]]
Entering the departure runway or line up and wait
All lights except landing lights [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24g]]
Takeoff clearance, or starting the roll at a nontowered field
Landing lights on [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24g]]

body.p: Night line up and wait: think about lining up about 3 feet left or right of the centerline so a landing pilot can tell you apart from the runway lights [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)(e)]]. Do not rely only on another aircraft's lights to judge what that pilot will do [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7h(1) NOTE]] [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(1) NOTE]].

bullets: Check the ramp with a flashlight before you get in; ladders, holes and chocks hide in the dark [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].
Clear the propeller area carefully; the beacon or flashing position lights help warn people nearby [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].
Taxi or landing light on to taxi, but some landing lights overheat or drain the battery if left on [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].
Taxi slowly and follow the painted lines. If position, route or runway do not look as expected, do not continue [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].
Hold or lock the brakes in the run-up; the airplane can creep forward unnoticed at night [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].
Pilot-controlled lighting: key the mike 7 times for full brightness; lights stay on 15 minutes from the last keying [[24:224|AFH 11-7]].

check.q: At night at a nontowered airport, when do your landing lights go on?
check.a: When you start the takeoff roll (at a towered field, when you get the takeoff clearance) [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24g]] [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)(f)]].

body.p: In low visibility the tower may not be able to see you, so nobody may be confirming that you follow the taxi instructions [[33:262|AIM 4-3-19a]]. Tell the controller at the first sign of becoming disoriented, and use extreme caution taxiing toward the sun [[33:262|AIM 4-3-19b]].

bullets: Use every resource: airport diagram, heading indicator, signs, markings and lights. Do all heads-down work while stopped [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(4)]].
While moving, give the airplane your full attention. Hold checklists and nonessential talk until stopped with the brakes set [[33:262|AIM 4-3-19d]].
Brief the low-visibility taxi chart if the airport has one, and listen for "hold short of the ILS critical area" [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(i)]].

head: Low-visibility aid
What it is
rows: SMGCS plan
Low-visibility taxi plan at airports with operations below 1,200 feet RVR, at two levels: below 1,200 to 500 feet RVR, and below 500 feet RVR [[33:262|AIM 4-3-19c]]
Geographic position marking
Pink circle with a number, left of the centerline, numbered in order along the route [[33:149|AIM 2-3-4g]]
Wide centerline
On a designated low-visibility route the centerline is 12 inches wide, outlined in black on light pavement [[20:74|AC 150/5340-1M 4.2.5.1.1]]
Taxiway centerline lights
Steady green, to guide you in low visibility [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10b]]
Stop bars and runway guard lights
Red stop bar confirms the clearance; flashing yellow guard lights mark the runway hold [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10d, e]]

check.q: Taxiing in fog you pass a pink circle marked "4A" on your left. What is it?
check.a: A geographic position marking on the low-visibility taxi route; it identifies where taxiing aircraft are when RVR is below 1,200 feet [[33:149|AIM 2-3-4g]].

chunks.title: Risk: distractions, bias, route changes, incursions

body.p: FAA data: about 65 percent of runway incursions are caused by pilots, and almost half of those by GA pilots. The three big causes are not following ATC instructions, not knowing the airport, and not following standard operating procedures [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

head: Hazard
How a professional handles it
rows: R1 Activities and distractions

14 CFR 135.100 is a Part 135 rule: there, taxi is a critical phase of flight with no nonessential duties or conversation [[6:33|14 CFR 135.100]]. It does not bind a Part 91 flight, but the FAA recommends the same sterile cockpit during GA taxi as good practice [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.5]]. Brief it, but invite anyone to speak up about a conflict [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(b)]]; passengers stay quiet from preflight until clear of the terminal area and at cruising altitude [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7c]]; phones off [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(j)]]
R2 Expectation and confirmation bias

Expectation bias: a wrong picture that persists despite evidence. Confirmation bias: brushing aside facts that do not fit. Fatigue makes both worse [[30:45|RMH 6-2]] [[30:46|RMH 6-3]]. Follow the clearance you actually got, not the one you expected [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(e) CAUTION]]
R3 Taxi route or runway change

Any change must be fully understood: stop if needed, write it, read it back and re-trace it [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]]. If position, route and runway do not all match, do not continue [[24:225|AFH 11-8]]
R4 Runway incursion

Read back every hold short and use a physical reminder, such as something hung on the yoke, since many incursions happen after a correct readback [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(3)]]. If you cannot comply safely, say "UNABLE" [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]]

body.p: Runway confusion is a type of incursion where you take off or land on the wrong runway or a taxiway. Its big risk factors are a complex airport, runway thresholds close together, and a runway used as a taxiway. Set the heading bug to the runway heading and confirm alignment before adding power [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

callout.text: Many errors happen when the pilot is off frequency or heads down [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(3) NOTE]]. Single pilot, once cleared onto the active runway, monitor only ATC until you are out of the Class B, C or D surface area [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b2]].

check.q: Name the three factors that make wrong-runway (runway confusion) events more likely.
check.a: Airport complexity, runway thresholds close to each other, and using a runway as a taxiway [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

bullets: Taxiing with a power setting that makes you control speed with the brakes [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
Forgetting to reset aileron and elevator after a turn changes the wind quadrant [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
Fast, sharp turns, especially from downwind toward upwind: side loads, tire damage, swerve or ground loop [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
Skipping the brake check, or doing it well after the airplane is rolling [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
Stopping with the nosewheel turned, which side-loads it and makes it harder to start straight [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
Any part of the airplane past a hold line without a clearance [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]].
Programming the GPS while moving instead of before taxi or while stopped [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(3) NOTE]].
Accepting a last-minute turnoff instruction you do not clearly understand [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(14)]].
Eyes fixed inside during the run-up while the parking brake slips [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

check.q: You keep turning the yoke into the wind but still feel the upwind wing lift on a tailwind leg. What is wrong?
check.a: On a quartering tailwind the upwind aileron goes DOWN (yoke away from the wind) with elevator down [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

scenario.title: Photo flight from an unfamiliar Class D airport
scenario.setup: You are a new commercial pilot hired to fly a photographer in a Cessna 182 from an airport you have never used. The tower closes at 2200; you will depart at dusk and return after it closes. A NOTAM says Taxiway Alpha is closed between A3 and A5. The airport diagram shows HS 1 where Taxiway Charlie crosses Runway 15-33. When you checked ATIS an hour ago, Runway 33 was in use, so you briefed a Runway 33 departure. The photographer is excited and wants to talk through the shot list while you taxi.

questions.q: Before engine start, what do you brief and set up?
questions.a: Diagram out, the expected route with hold short lines, crossings and HS 1, when you will do checklists, and flaps, trim and GPS done before moving [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(a), (c), (d), (g)]]. Ask the photographer for a sterile cockpit but to speak up about any conflict [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(b)]] [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7c]].

questions.q: Ground says: "Skylane 735KD, Runway 6, taxi via Alpha, cross Runway 33." What two things should catch your attention?
questions.a: First, the clearance routes you over the part of Alpha the NOTAM says is closed, so ask the controller to verify it [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b(1)(c)]] [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]]. Second, the runway is 6, not the 33 you briefed: expectation bias could make you hear what you planned [[30:46|RMH 6-3]]. Follow the clearance actually received [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(e) CAUTION]].

questions.q: Ground amends your route to "via Charlie, cross Runway 33 at Charlie." How do you handle the change?
questions.a: Stop if needed, write the new route, read back the runway and the crossing, and re-trace it on the diagram, noting HS 1 [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]] [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]]. If anything does not match what you see, do not continue [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].

questions.q: At the Runway 33 hold line, cleared to cross, you see an airplane on short final for 33 and the photographer keeps talking. What now?
questions.a: Do not cross. Stop and ask ATC to clarify; you must be positive of the clearance and scan the runway and final even after being cleared [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(4)]] [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]]. Remind the passenger of the sterile cockpit [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7c]].

questions.q: You land on Runway 6 at 2215 with the tower closed and must cross Runway 33 to reach the FBO. What is your procedure?
questions.a: Use the CTAF: listen, announce, and remember some aircraft have no radio. Scan the full runway and its approach and departure paths, and cross only when it is clear with no one on final [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(12)]] [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]]. Turn on all exterior lights to cross [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24f]].

questions.q: The FBO ramp is dark and unfamiliar. How do you avoid a taxi mishap there?
questions.a: Taxi slowly, follow the painted lines, and use the taxi light without blinding others. If you doubt your clearance from any object, stop and check [[24:225|AFH 11-8]] [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

skills.do: Copy and correctly read back the taxi clearance: runway assignment, every crossing, hold shorts and line up and wait, with full call sign.
skills.practice: Copy recorded or chair-flown ground clearances in shorthand ("/" for hold short, "X" for cross) and read them back aloud [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e(2)]].

skills.do: Keep the airport diagram in view and always know your position and the next turn, crossing or hot spot.
skills.practice: Before each flight trace the route and hot spots, then confirm each taxiway with the heading indicator as you taxi [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7d(1)]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7g(1)]].

skills.do: Hold the correct aileron and elevator for the wind on every leg of the route.
skills.practice: Before each turn, work out the new wind quadrant and set the controls as you roll out of the turn [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

skills.do: Complete the POH taxi checklist and the flight instrument checks.
skills.practice: Do the instrument checks on a straight, quiet stretch, not at a complex intersection [[24:58|AFH 2-21]] [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(a)]].

skills.do: Test both brakes as soon as the airplane starts moving.
skills.practice: Make it automatic on every taxi: roll, throttle back, one brake, then the other [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

skills.do: Control speed with the throttle and direction with the rudder, using brakes sparingly.
skills.practice: Practice long downwind taxis at minimum power with only occasional braking [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

skills.do: Follow signs, markings, light signals and ATC instructions exactly as issued.
skills.practice: Name each sign and marking aloud as you pass it, and review light gun signals for aircraft on the ground [[1:359|PHAK 14-25]].

skills.do: Stop with no part of the airplane past a hold line; when exiting, keep going until the whole airplane is past it.
skills.practice: Have your instructor check your stopping point at each hold line, and after landing check that the tail is clear [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]] [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(11)]].

quiz.q: How often is the Chart Supplement revised?
options: Every 28 days
Once a year
Every 6 months
Every 56 days
quiz.why: The Chart Supplement is published in seven regional books revised every 56 days [[1:337|PHAK 14-3]].

quiz.q: Which regulation says you need an ATC clearance to taxi on a taxiway at an airport with an operating control tower?
quiz.why: 91.129(i) prohibits operating on a runway or taxiway, or taking off or landing, without an appropriate clearance at a towered airport [[60:454|14 CFR 91.129(i)]]. 91.209 is aircraft lights [[60:491|14 CFR 91.209]].

quiz.q: You are taxiing on a parallel taxiway well away from Runway 15 and see a red sign reading "15-APCH". What does it mark?
options: A direction sign toward the Runway 15 threshold
The end of the usable taxiway
A holding position protecting the Runway 15 approach area
The edge of the Runway 15 safety area for exiting aircraft
quiz.why: A runway approach area holding position sign shows the approach end runway number, a dash and "APCH". Hold there when told to hold short of the Runway 15 approach [[33:163|AIM 2-3-8b2]] [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a3]].

quiz.q: Where are enhanced taxiway centerline dashes painted?
options: On every taxiway leading to any holding position
Between the runway hold line and the runway edge
Only on taxiways that lead directly onto a runway, for up to 150 feet before the hold line
On runways that are also used as taxiways
quiz.why: They run up to 150 feet before a runway holding position marking and are used only on taxiways that directly enter a runway; the part between the hold line and runway is not enhanced [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]] [[20:74|AC 150/5340-1M 4.3]] [[20:75|AC 150/5340-1M 4.3]].

quiz.q: In low visibility ATC clears you across a runway, but the stop bar in front of you is still lit red. You should:
options: Cross, because the ATC clearance overrides the lights
Cross slowly with all lights on
Flash your landing light and cross
Stay stopped and contact ATC
quiz.why: Never cross a red illuminated stop bar, even with a clearance to proceed [[33:134|AIM 2-1-10e CAUTION]].

quiz.q: Who has the final authority to accept or decline a land and hold short clearance?
options: The tower controller
The pilot in command
The airport manager
Whoever is first in the landing sequence
quiz.why: The PIC has final authority to accept or decline any LAHSO clearance and is expected to decline if safety would be compromised [[33:254|AIM 4-3-11b3]].

quiz.q: You are taxiing on heading 180 with the wind from 230 at 15 knots. How should you hold the controls?
options: Yoke left and forward
Yoke left, elevator neutral
Yoke right and forward
Yoke right, elevator neutral
quiz.why: 230 - 180 = 50: right front, a quartering headwind. Upwind (right) aileron up, so yoke right, with neutral elevator [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

quiz.q: Why does the run-up need extra attention at night?
options: Engines produce less power at night
Magneto checks are not valid in the dark
The airplane can creep forward without you noticing
Taxiway edge lights hide the hold line
quiz.why: At night forward movement is hard to see, so hold or lock the brakes and watch for creeping during the run-up [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].

quiz.q: According to FAA data in the PHAK, roughly what share of runway incursions are caused by pilots?
options: About 65 percent
About 35 percent
About 15 percent
About 90 percent
quiz.why: About 65 percent of runway incursions are caused by pilots, and almost half of those by GA pilots [[1:366|PHAK 14-32]].

takeaways: Plan the taxi like a phase of flight: Chart Supplement, diagram, NOTAMs, ATIS and hot spots before engine start.
Read back runway, crossings, hold shorts and LUAW with full call sign; copy complex routes in shorthand.
Red sign or red light: stop until cleared. RWSL and stop bars never give you a clearance, but a red one always stops you.
No part of the airplane past a hold line without a clearance; when exiting, the whole airplane must clear it.
LAHSO is your call as PIC: know the ALD before you go and say "unable" early.
Hold the yoke into a headwind and away from (and forward in) a tailwind, and reset it after every turn.
At night and in low visibility: slow down, heads-down work only when stopped, and tell ATC the moment you are unsure.
cfi_notes: AC 91-73B asks instructors to limit cockpit instruction while taxiing [[7:17|AC 91-73B App 3]]. Teach in the briefing; let the student run a sterile cockpit on the ground.
Have commercial applicants give a spoken pre-taxi briefing using the AC 91-73B Appendix 2 card: taxi route, hot spots and departure items [[7:15|AC 91-73B App 2]].
Students mix up clearance bar lights and in-pavement runway guard lights; the AIM notes some airports have three or five yellow lights at runway intersections [[33:133|AIM 2-1-10d NOTE]].

Two LAHSO limits come only from the PHAK list: generally not at night, and not on wet runways [[1:345|PHAK 14-11]]. AIM 4-3-11 says neither; its only weather limit is a 1,000-foot ceiling and 3 statute miles [[33:256|AIM 4-3-11c5]]. Teach AIM 4-3-11 as the controlling guidance and always label the night and wet-runway points as PHAK-only.
The MRY diagram in AFH Figure 2-14 is dated 2012 and is for training only; always use the current Terminal Procedures diagram [[24:55|AFH 2-18]].
AC 91-73B and the PHAK still say "Notices to Airmen"; the ACS uses "Notices to Air Missions". It is the same NOTAM system.

Examiners like to probe RWSL meaning, approach-area hold signs, LAHSO acceptance and route changes at a hot spot. AC 91-73B is for single-pilot operations; two-pilot crews use AC 120-74 [[7:1|AC 91-73B 1 NOTE]].
gaps: POH/AFM items (taxi checklist, landing light duty limits, brake system details and landing distance for LAHSO decisions) are not in the sources.
AC 120-57 (low-visibility SMGCS) and AC 120-74 (two-pilot taxi procedures) are referenced but not included, so low-visibility taxi chart symbols are not covered.
Chart Supplement legend decoding and current hot spot listings for real airports are not in the sources; the Chart Users' Guide gives only the symbol.
Multiengine (AMEL) taxi items are not taught; this lesson is single-engine land only.
Tailwheel-specific taxi technique (AFH Ch 14) is only touched on (elevator position in a headwind).

activities.title: True or false: clearances and readbacks
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: If you read back a hold short instruction correctly, you have done everything needed to avoid that incursion.
cards.why: Many runway incursions happen even after a correct "hold short" readback; use a physical reminder too [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(3)]].

cards.s: ATC is required to get a readback of every runway hold short instruction.
cards.why: ATC must obtain a readback of all runway hold short instructions [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a7 NOTE]] [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b1 NOTE]].

cards.s: At a towered airport you need a clearance to taxi on a taxiway, not only on a runway.
cards.why: 91.129(i) covers operating on a runway or taxiway at an airport with an operating tower [[60:454|14 CFR 91.129(i)]].

cards.s: Ground says "cleared to taxi" whenever it approves your taxi.
cards.why: To avoid confusion, ATC does not use the word "cleared" with taxi authorizations [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]].

cards.s: If you are unsure of a clearance, the regulations require you to ask ATC right away.
cards.why: A pilot uncertain of an ATC clearance shall immediately request clarification [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]].

cards.s: Your first call to ground needs only your call sign and "ready to taxi".
cards.why: Give identification, location, VFR or IFR and first landing point, plus the ATIS code [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18d1]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(2)]].

cards.s: A controller may give progressive taxi instructions even if you did not ask.
cards.why: Progressive instructions may be issued when the controller thinks it necessary because of traffic or field conditions [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b3]].

activities.title: Name the signs and markings
activities.intro: Drag each name to its numbered pin.

activities.title: What is this light telling you?
activities.intro: Tap a clue, then tap where it belongs.
buckets: Red: stop, runway unsafe or clearance not confirmed
Blue or green: taxi path guidance

activities.title: Told to hold short, then cross Runway 9: put it in order
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: See yellow dashes beside the centerline and slow down
Stop with no part of the airplane past the solid hold lines
Hear "cross Runway 9" and read it back with call sign and runway
Scan the full length of Runway 9 and its final approach
Cross promptly, without stopping on the runway
Keep rolling until the whole airplane is past the far-side hold marking

activities.title: Heading and wind: set the yoke
activities.intro: Tap a heading and wind, then the yoke position.

activities.title: Work the numbers on the ground
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer.

items.q: Takeoff Hold Lights start 375 feet from the departure threshold and extend 1,500 feet. How far from the threshold do they end?
You taxi at 10 knots (about 17 feet per second) and pass the first enhanced centerline dash at its maximum distance from the hold line. About how many seconds until you reach the hold line?
items.why: Enhanced centerlines run up to 150 feet before the hold line. 150 / 17 = about 8.8, so about 9 seconds [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]].

items.q: Tower told you to line up and wait with no reason given, and nothing visible explains the wait. 50 seconds have passed. How many more seconds before you should call ATC?
items.why: Expect a call within 90 seconds; if none, call ATC. 90 - 50 = 40 seconds [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(9)]].

items.q: At a nontowered field you keyed the mike 7 times at 21:40 to turn on the lights. It is now 21:52 and you are still taxiing. How many minutes until the lights may go out unless you key again?
items.why: Pilot-controlled lights stay on 15 minutes from the last keying: 21:40 + 15 = 21:55, minus 21:52 = 3 minutes [[24:224|AFH 11-7]].

items.q: The 2012 MRY airport diagram in AFH Figure 2-14 (figure 1) lists Runway 10R-28L as 7,616 feet long. Using that value, you land on 10R and pass the "4" distance remaining sign. About how many feet of runway have you used?
items.why: The 7,616 feet comes from that 2012 training diagram, not a current chart [[24:55|AFH Figure 2-14]]. The sign shows thousands of feet of landing runway remaining: 4,000 feet left. 7,616 - 4,000 = 3,616 feet used [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]].

activities.title: Dusk departure: one decision at a time
activities.intro: You are flying N735KD, a Cessna 182, on a paid photo flight from a busy towered airport at dusk. Your passenger is the photographer, and another Cessna, N735KB, is on the same ground frequency.

steps.s: Ground: "N735KD, Runway 28R, taxi via Bravo, Charlie, hold short of Runway 1L at Charlie." Your passenger is still talking about camera angles.
options: Reply "Roger, 735KD" and start rolling
Start taxiing and read back once the passenger stops talking
Ask for progressive taxi instead of reading back
Read back "N735KD, Runway 28R, via Bravo, Charlie, hold short of Runway 1L at Charlie" and write it down
steps.why: Read back runway assignment and hold short with full call sign, not "Roger" [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]]. Writing it down guards against forgetting part of it [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e]].

steps.s: Rolling on Bravo, you realize the GPS flight plan is not loaded.
options: Program it now while taxiing straight
Wait until you are stopped, such as at the run-up area, to program it
Hand the GPS to the photographer to program
Skip it and load it after takeoff
steps.why: Heads-down work like GPS programming belongs before taxi or while stopped; many errors happen during heads-down tasks [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(3) NOTE]] [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(g)]].

steps.s: Nearing Charlie you see yellow dashes beside the centerline and flashing yellow lights ahead. You hear: "Cessna 735KB, cross Runway 1L at Charlie."
options: Cross; it was almost certainly for you
Say "crossing" and go
Hold short and ask ATC to confirm who was cleared
Flash your landing light and cross
steps.why: With a similar call sign on frequency, do not act on a clearance that may be for the other aircraft [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(6)]]. When in doubt, ask ATC [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b1]].

steps.s: ATC: "N735KD, cross Runway 1L at Charlie." As you reach the hold line, red lights come on in the pavement along the taxiway centerline toward the runway.
options: Cross; you have a clearance
Back up and find another route
Cross quickly before traffic arrives
Stop at the hold line and contact ATC
steps.why: Red Runway Entrance Lights mean the runway is unsafe. Stop at the hold line or stay stopped and contact ATC if your clearance conflicts [[33:127|AIM 2-1-6b]].

steps.s: After crossing, ground says: "N735KD, change of runway, Runway 28L, taxi via Delta."
options: Stop if needed, write and read back the new route, and re-trace it on the diagram
Keep going and look for Delta on the way
Ask to keep Runway 28R because you briefed it
Reply "Wilco" and turn at the next taxiway
steps.why: Any change to the taxi route must be fully understood and re-checked on the diagram [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]]. Follow the clearance actually received, not the one you briefed [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(e) CAUTION]].

steps.s: Tower: "N735KD, Runway 28L, line up and wait." No reason is given and nothing is visible on the runway. 90 seconds go by with no call.
options: Begin the takeoff roll
Keep waiting quietly
Contact the tower
Exit at the nearest taxiway
steps.why: If no call comes within 90 seconds of a LUAW instruction, contact ATC, and watch for light gun signals in case of a radio problem [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(9) and NOTE]] [[1:369|PHAK 14-35]].

final_quiz.q: You will taxi at MRY (figure). What does the caution printed on the airport diagram require?
options: A call to clearance delivery before taxi
Progressive taxi for every departure
Readback of all runway holding instructions
Holding short of the ILS critical area at all times
final_quiz.why: The MRY diagram caution says to be alert to runway crossing clearances and that readback of all runway holding instructions is required [[24:55|AFH Figure 2-14]]. That matches the AIM readback list [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]].

final_quiz.q: Your route at a large airport crosses three runways. How will ATC normally give the crossings?
options: All three in the initial taxi clearance
Not at all; the runway assignment covers them
Only for runways that are active
One at a time, after you have crossed the previous one
final_quiz.why: ATC must issue explicit instructions for each runway, normally one at a time after the previous crossing, except closely spaced runways under 1,000 feet apart. This applies to active, inactive and closed runways [[1:368|PHAK 14-34]] [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]].

final_quiz.q: On rollout you pass a sign with a white "3" on a black background. What does it tell you?
options: You are 3,000 feet from the threshold
About 3,000 feet of runway remain
Exit at the third taxiway
You are on Runway 3
final_quiz.why: Runway distance remaining signs show the landing runway left in thousands of feet [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]] [[19:13|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]].

final_quiz.q: After landing you turn off and pass a yellow sign with a black graphic beside the hold marking. What does it tell you?
options: You may not enter this area
A runway holding position is ahead
When you are past it, you are clear of the runway
An ILS critical area begins here
final_quiz.why: The runway boundary sign is seen by pilots leaving the runway and helps them decide when they are clear of it [[33:166|AIM 2-3-9a3]] [[19:12|AC 150/5340-18H, Glossary of Sign Types]].

final_quiz.q: Tower: "Cleared to land Runway 9, hold short of Runway 13." You know your landing distance will not fit the ALD. What is the best response?
options: Say "unable" and request the full length or another runway
Accept and plan a go-around
Accept, then land long if needed
Accept, then exit early if you can
final_quiz.why: If you cannot safely comply, tell ATC promptly, ideally before the clearance is issued, and request full length or another runway [[33:255|AIM 4-3-11b5]]. Use the word "UNABLE" [[1:367|PHAK 14-33]].

final_quiz.q: What is the minimum weather for ATC to issue a LAHSO clearance?
options: 500-foot ceiling and 1 mile
1,000-foot ceiling and 3 statute miles
3,000-foot ceiling and 5 miles
800-foot ceiling and 2 miles
final_quiz.why: Pilots should only receive a LAHSO clearance with at least a 1,000-foot ceiling and 3 statute miles visibility [[33:256|AIM 4-3-11c5]] [[1:344|PHAK 14-10]].

final_quiz.q: You are in position on the runway waiting for takeoff clearance when a double row of red lights lights up ahead of you. What does it mean?
options: The runway ahead is occupied or about to be; stay stopped and call ATC if your clearance conflicts
You are cleared for takeoff when they go out
The runway end is 1,000 feet ahead
LAHSO is in effect
final_quiz.why: Red Takeoff Hold Lights mean it is unsafe to take off because the runway is or will be occupied. Stop or stay stopped and contact ATC if any clearance conflicts [[33:128|AIM 2-1-6c]].

final_quiz.q: Taxiing at night you see alternating green and yellow centerline lights curving off the runway. What do they tell you?
options: You are still inside the runway environment or ILS critical area
A taxiway that is closed
The edge of the ramp
A low-visibility route ahead
final_quiz.why: Lead-off and lead-on lights alternate green and yellow to warn you that you are within the runway environment or ILS critical area [[33:126|AIM 2-1-5c, d]].

final_quiz.q: At a nontowered airport, when should you self-announce on the CTAF for departure?
options: Only when entering the runway
Only at 10 miles out
Only if other traffic is heard
Before taxiing and before taxiing onto the runway for departure
final_quiz.why: The recommended outbound calls are before taxiing and before taxiing on the runway for departure [[1:337|PHAK Figure 14-1]].

final_quiz.q: You taxi on heading 090 with the wind from 320 at 18 knots. How do you hold the controls?
options: Yoke right and forward
Yoke right, elevator neutral
Yoke left and forward
Yoke left, elevator neutral
final_quiz.why: 320 - 090 = 230: left rear, a quartering tailwind. Upwind (left) aileron down and elevator down, so yoke right and forward [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

final_quiz.q: Later you fly for a Part 135 operator. Under 14 CFR 135.100, which phase of flight allows only duties needed for safe operation?
options: Only takeoff and landing
Only flight below 10,000 feet
All ground operations involving taxi, takeoff and landing, and flight below 10,000 feet except cruise
Only the time on the runway
final_quiz.why: Critical phases of flight include all ground operations involving taxi, takeoff and landing, and all other flight below 10,000 feet except cruise [[6:33|14 CFR 135.100]]. This is a Part 135 rule; under Part 91 a sterile cockpit on the ground is FAA-recommended good practice, not a regulation [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.5]].

final_quiz.q: You briefed a taxi via Bravo, but ground clears you via Delta. Which response follows AC 91-73B?
options: Follow the Delta clearance you received, read it back and re-check the diagram
Taxi via Bravo, since you briefed it
Ask ground to give you Bravo again
Taxi via either one; both reach the runway
final_quiz.why: A pitfall of planning is setting expectations; follow the clearance actually received, not the one you expected [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(e) CAUTION]], and make sure any change is fully understood [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]].

final_quiz.q: RVR is 1,000 feet and your taxi route has pink circles with numbers on the left of the centerline. What are they?
options: Hot spot markers
Geographic position markings on a low-visibility taxi route
Run-up area numbers
Parking spot numbers
final_quiz.why: Geographic position markings identify taxiing aircraft positions on SMGCS low-visibility routes when RVR is below 1,200 feet; they sit left of the centerline [[33:149|AIM 2-3-4g]].

final_quiz.q: Single pilot, you are cleared onto the active runway in Class D airspace. What should you monitor until you leave the surface area?
options: ATIS for weather changes
Only assigned ATC communications
Your company frequency
The next airport's CTAF
final_quiz.why: Single-pilot aircraft should monitor only assigned ATC communications after being cleared onto the active runway until out of the Class B, C or D surface area [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b2]].
